DIP28_2764.name: JEDEC 2764/27C64
DIP28_2764.comment: infoic.xml pin map 21, which leaves pin 26 unbonded: pin 26 NC, and pin 27 PGM. The host sends PGM as the rw line, so the firmware holds it high for read. See datasheets/TMS2764.pdf.

DIP28_27128.name: JEDEC 27128/27C128
DIP28_27128.comment: infoic.xml pin map 22 (pin_map 0x00000c16), which bonds pin 26 as A13. Pin 27 is PGM; the host sends it as the rw line.

DIP28_27011.name: 27011 page-addressed EPROM
DIP28_27011.comment: infoic.xml pin map 22 with pin_map 0x90000c16, which only the 27011 rows carry. Connectivity is <maps> index 22. The pin functions are the 27128 functions these rows had before the split; no 27011 datasheet was found to confirm them. Page selection is not implemented (henols/firestarter#136).

DIP28_6264.name: JEDEC 28-pin SRAM/FRAM (6264 family)
DIP28_6264.comment: 13-bit JEDEC parallel SRAM/FRAM: A0-A12 on the 2764 address pins, WE on pin 27, pin 1 NC. Pin 26 is CS2 (active high) on 6264-class SRAM such as HM6264, W2464 and M48T08 (E2), and NC on FM1608 and DS1225, so it is held high. The generator chooses this map by the infoic address width (13 bits or less); a 15-bit part uses DIP28_28C256, where pin 26 is A13.

DIP32_STD.name: JEDEC 32-Pin Standard
DIP32_STD.comment: Standard 32-pin UV-EPROM layout (27C010/27C020/27C040 family). VPP on pin 1, PGM (where applicable) on pin 31; A18 takes over pin 31 on 27C040. NOT correct for 5V flash (AM29F040/SST39SF040 family — those have A18 at pin 1, WE at pin 31 — see DIP32_SST39SF040).

DIP32_SST39SF040.name: JEDEC 32-pin 5V Flash (SST39SF040/AM29F040 family)
DIP32_SST39SF040.comment: Per piersfinlayson/one-rom (datasheet-verified): SST39SF040 and same-family 4Mbit/8Mbit 5V flash chips have A18 at pin 1 (NOT VPP) and WE at pin 31 (NOT address bus). Distinct from DIP32_STD (UV-EPROM 27C040 layout) where pins 1 and 31 are swapped. Covers ~47 chips at (pin_count=32, pm_idx=13, protocol_id=0x06): AM29F040, SST39SF040, A29040, EN29F040, MX29F040, etc. — all 5V single-supply flash.

DIP32_27C020.name: JEDEC 32-pin UV-EPROM ≤256K (27C010/27C020 family — PGM on pin 31)
DIP32_27C020.comment: Scoped pinout for 0x08 protocol chips with mem_size ≤ 262144 (≤256K — A18 bit 18 = mask 0x40000 unused). Per AM27C020.pdf: pin 1 = VPP (12.75V programming voltage), pin 31 = PGM (active-LOW program enable, NOT A18). On 256K and smaller parts, address bit 18 is never set, so pin 31 is always the PGM control, never an address line. Scope: ONLY assigned by resolve_pinout_key to proto_id=0x08 && mem_size<=262144 (D-02/D-04 alias guard). The 512K AM27C040 and 1M AM27C080 legitimately use pin 31 = A18 and MUST stay on DIP32_STD. CR-01 CORRECTED FIX (2026-07-01, operator schematic study): pin 31 is the distinct RW line — CTRL_READ_WRITE (physical bit 0x40) — DISTINCT from P1/VPP (CTRL_VPP_P1_ENABLE, physical bit 0x08) on BOTH legacy Rev 0/1 AND Rev 2 layouts (revision-invariant; the earlier CR-01 fork worry about a Rev-2 P1/PGM alias was a misdiagnosis — that alias is CTRL_ADDRESS_LINE_18_REV2/CTRL_VPP_P1_ENABLE_REV2 sharing 0x08, which this fix never touches). pgm-pin:[31] goes on the wire as rw-pin, because get_bus_config sends the pgm-pin of a map that has no rw-pin as its rw line. That is the SAME rw_line mechanism as the DIP32_SST39SF040 WE on pin 31: the host resolves pin 31 -> pin_conversions[32][31] = 22 -> config.rw_line = 22, and the firmware's mem_util_remap_address_bus / mem_util_calculate_top_address_register fold bus line 22 into the CONTROL register's CTRL_READ_WRITE (0x40) bit, held at the program-active VIL level for the full write (WRITE_FLAG=0) pulse. Static-high-pins is RULED OUT as the PGM vehicle (Q1, 2026-06-30) — static_high_mask ORs HIGH into the bus line with no inversion in the RURP latch path, but PGM program-active is VIL (LOW). The rw line is the correct mechanism: it is the missing assignment that makes pin 31 a DELIBERATELY-driven /PGM (=/WE) write strobe instead of merely unassigned/floating. Whether this flips bits on the seated AM27C020 remains the Phase-99 empirical gate; this pinout delivers the corrected host bus-config, not a silicon proof.

DIP32_27C301.name: Mask-ROM-compatible 32-pin UV-EPROM (27C301 / 27C1000 — OE on pin 2, A16 on pin 24)
DIP32_27C301.comment: infoic.xml pin map 12 with protocol 0x08 and variant_lo 0x00. Only MBM27C1000, MBM27C2000, HN27C301G, HN27C301AG and M27C1000 carry it; variant_lo 0x01 in the same map is the JEDEC 27C020 layout. Pin functions are from datasheets/MBM27C1000.pdf (page 4-61 pin assignment, page 4-63 pin description): pin 1 VPP, pin 2 OE, pin 22 CE, pin 24 A16, pin 31 PGM, pin 30 NC. one-rom chip-types.json type 27C301 (aliases 27C1000, 27C100) gives the same OE and A16 pins. JEDEC 27C010/27C020 swap pins 2 and 24, so on DIP32_27C020 these parts drive OE high whenever A16 is 1 (henols/firestarter#70). Pin 30 is A17 for the 256K MBM27C2000 row: <maps> index 12 bonds it, and it is the only bonded pin that has no other function on this layout. No MBM27C2000 datasheet is vendored to confirm it.

DIP32_27C801.name: JEDEC 32-pin UV-EPROM 1M (27C080 / M27C801 — A19 on pin 1, VPP on pin 24)
DIP32_27C801.comment: Per piersfinlayson/one-rom docs/CHIP-TYPES.md (datasheet-verified): the 8 Mbit 27C080/M27C801 class has 20 address lines (A0-A19) with A19 at pin 1, and VPP at pin 24 shared with /OE — the same OE/VPP sharing DIP28_27512 uses at pin 22. /PGM is pin 22 shared with /CE. Distinct from DIP32_STD (27C040 class: pin 1 = VPP, pin 31 = A18, 19 address lines) and from DIP32_27C020 (pin 31 = PGM). Assigned by resolve_pinout_key to pin_count=32 && pm_idx=12 && proto_id=0x08 && variant_lo=0x03 — the eight 1 MB rows AM27C080, AM27LV080, AT27C080, M27C801 (x2), MX27C8000, MX27C8000A, UPD27C8001. HARDWARE: A19 at pin 1 means socket pin 1 carries an address line, and on Rev 2.x shields socket pin 1 is also the VPP-enable line (JP5 = A19_CUT bridges it to the switched VPP node). JP5 must be cut for these parts, per the shield silkscreen.

DIP28_28C256.name: JEDEC 28-pin 5V parallel EEPROM (28C256 family)
DIP28_28C256.comment: Per piersfinlayson/one-rom (datasheet-verified): 28C256 family has 15 address pins (A0-A14), with A14 at pin 1 (NOT VPP) and WE at pin 27 (NOT PGM). 5V single-supply, no programming voltage. Distinct from DIP28_2764 (UV-EPROM layout) which has VPP at pin 1 and PGM at pin 27. Covers ~8 chips at (pin_count=28, pm_idx=20, protocol_id=0x07): AT28C256, AT28C256E/F, HN58C256, HN58C256AP, etc. Routes through configure_eeprom28c after WARNING-5 algo override OR directly via pm_idx-based pinout selection.

DIP24_6116.name: JEDEC 24-pin 5V SRAM (6116/6264-style)
DIP24_6116.comment: Per piersfinlayson/one-rom (datasheet-verified): 6116 SRAM has 11 address pins (A0-A10) with A10=pin 19, CE=18, OE=20, WE=21. 5V single-supply, no programming voltage. Used by 6116-class 2KB SRAM chips. Covers the (pin_count=24, pm_idx=0, protocol_id=0x27) group + any other JEDEC 24-pin SRAM/FRAM with 6116-compatible pinout.

DIP24_2532.name: TI 2532 (4KB) — non-JEDEC 24-pin UV-EPROM
DIP24_2532.comment: TI/Motorola 2532 is a 4KB (4096x8) 24-pin UV-EPROM with a NON-JEDEC pinout that differs from the JEDEC 2732 (DIP24_2732). On the 2532: VPP=pin 21, A11=pin 18, !PD/PGM=pin 20 (chip-enable / power-down-program), VCC=pin 24, GND=pin 12. The JEDEC 2732 instead puts OE/VPP on pin 20, A11 on pin 21, and CE on pin 18 — so the two layouts must NOT be conflated (VPP on pin 21 vs pin 20 is a 12-25V-to-wrong-pin hardware-damage path). Source: TI 2532 datasheet pin assignment (committed 2516/2532-family scan under datasheets/0x0B-EPROM-LEGACY/2516_EPROM.pdf, which is the TI 2500-series UV-EPROM family doc covering the 2516/2532 lineage). vpp-pin=21 satisfies the GATE-03 structural VPP guard for the 0x0B legacy EPROM handler. Tentative leaf layout — bench-validation required (carries the same UNVERIFIED posture as the 2516 supplement row).

DIP24_2816.name: JEDEC 24-pin 5V parallel EEPROM (AT28C16/AT28C04 family)
DIP24_2816.comment: AT28C16/AT28C04/28C16A-class 24-pin 5V single-supply parallel EEPROMs. Same physical layout as DIP24_6116 SRAM (WE=pin 21, OE=pin 20, CE=pin 18, VCC=pin 24, GND=pin 12). NO vpp-pin — configure_eeprom28c is 5V-only (SDP-disable + DQ7 page-write polling; VPP regulator is never asserted). Over-allocated to A0-A10 (11 address bits = AT28C16 maximum); AT28C04 has 9 address lines and firmware restricts driving via mem_size. Source: Atmel AT28C16 datasheet Table 1 (pin description). Pin 21=WE, NOT VPP — the DIP24_2716 (UV-EPROM) layout has VPP=pin 21; this layout does NOT.

DIP28_28C64.name: JEDEC 28-pin 5V parallel EEPROM 8K (28C64 family)
DIP28_28C64.comment: Per piersfinlayson/one-rom (datasheet-verified): 28C64 has 13 address pins (A0-A12, same as 2764 EPROM), CE=20, OE=22, WE=27, pin 1=NC (or /busy on some variants). 5V single-supply, no programming voltage. Distinct from DIP28_2764 (UV-EPROM layout) — pin 27 is WE (not PGM), pin 1 is NC (not VPP). Covers (pin_count=28, pm_idx=19, protocol_id=0x07) group: AM28C64A/B/E, etc. Routes through configure_eeprom28c via WARNING-5 algo flip.

DIP32_28C040.name: JEDEC 32-pin 5V parallel EEPROM (28C512/28C010/28C020/28C040 family)
DIP32_28C040.comment: infoic.xml <maps> 9, 11 and 13, which every 32-pin protocol 0x0D row uses, bond pin 31 and never pin 30 on the 28C512/28C010 maps, so WE is pin 31. A16 is pin 2, A17 pin 30 and A18 pin 1, as on DIP32_SST39SF040. Each row's nc_pins (from <maps>) removes the address pins its chip does not bond. one-rom chip-types.json gives its 28C512 write = 30, but its own SST39SF040 on the same layout gives 31, so it is not used here.
